entries.title: Cups Overflow: When your printer spills more than Ink
entries.description: Elastic Security Labs discusses detection and mitigation strategies for vulnerabilities in the CUPS printing system, which allow unauthenticated attackers to exploit the system via IPP and mDNS, resulting in remote code execution (RCE) on UNIX-based systems such as Linux, macOS, BSDs, ChromeOS, and Solaris.

entries.title: Betting on Bots: Investigating Linux malware, crypto mining, and gambling API abuse
entries.description: The REF6138 campaign involved cryptomining, DDoS attacks, and potential money laundering via gambling APIs, highlighting the attackers' use of evolving malware and stealthy communication channels.

entries.title: Storm on the Horizon: Inside the AJCloud IoT Ecosystem
entries.description: Wi-Fi cameras are popular due to their affordability and convenience but often have security vulnerabilities that can be exploited.

entries.title: Code of Conduct: DPRK’s Python-fueled intrusions into secured networks
entries.description: Investigating the DPRK’s strategic use of Python and carefully crafted social engineering, this publication sheds light on how they breach highly secure networks with evolving and effective cyber attacks.

entries.title: Kernel ETW is the best ETW
entries.description: This research focuses on the importance of native audit logs in secure-by-design software, emphasizing the need for kernel-level ETW logging over user-mode hooks to enhance anti-tamper protections.

entries.title: Elastic releases the Detection Engineering Behavior Maturity Model
entries.description: Using this maturity model, security teams can make structured, measurable, and iteritive improvements to their detection engineering teams..
